notes: Site: Shopify store, plain direct HTTP fetch worked, no WAF/Claude-disallow. Navigation discovery: main nav includes 'NEW ARRIVALS' (banner text 'SHOP NEW') pointing to /collections/new-arrivals. Full sitemap_collections_1.xml enumerated (1952 URLs) and grep-scanned for new-/just-in/latest/recently-added terms. Found /collections/new-arrivals (nav-linked), /collections/new-items and /collections/newest-products as genuine 'new products' candidates; also many brand/product-line collections whose handles merely contain the word 'new' as part of a proper noun (new-works [a brand], menu-new-norm, blu-dot-new-standard, cane-line-newman, cane-line-newport, new-gus-modern, new-lighting) -- these were excluded without further inspection since they name a specific vendor/product line, not a 'recently added to catalogue' concept. QTY METHOD: exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json pagination (limit=250) deduplicated by product handle. New Arrivals: 3 pages (250+250+102), 602 unique products, zero duplicates -- site's own products_count metadata reports 816, not used (see this company's Bestsellers file for the products_count-unreliability finding on this same site). New Items: 1 page, 155 unique products (metadata reports 452, not used). Confirmed New Items is a genuinely distinct listing, not an alias of New Arrivals, by sampling the first 20 product handles of each: completely disjoint product sets (New Items sample was almost entirely one vendor, 'aytm'; New Arrivals sample spanned New Works, Sika Design, Louis Poulsen, Ethnicraft, Tom Dixon) -- kept as two separate rows per the brief's multiple-PLP rule. Newest Products (/collections/newest-products) checked and confirmed empty: products.json returns 0 products and collection metadata products_count=0 -- dropped per the drop-zero-product-listing rule.
